chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Sin Metal is the jewel, refined and selective. You don't fall easily, so if you're in a situationship, this person impressed you. You might stay because you like the idea of them, or because asking for more feels like exposing yourself in an unflattering light. You'd rather be elegantly casual than visibly invested. Ask yourself honestly: is the casualness real, or is it a very beautiful cover for wanting something you're scared to ask for? Only you know, and you probably already do. Write the answer in one honest line, just for yourself. Nobody else needs to see it.
text.what-you-want: You want to be treasured. Seen in detail. Chosen with intention, not by default. Sin Metal has high standards, and that includes how you're treated by the people you let close. You may have lowered them temporarily to keep this light and easy. Write down what you'd want if you weren't worried about looking like too much. That list is your real standard, and it's not too high. It's simply specific, which is what good taste looks like when it's applied to love. Keep the list somewhere private and read it before your next date with them. See how it compares to what's actually happening.
text.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you analyse them with precision and then pretend you didn't notice anything. Sin Metal stays composed on the outside while quietly scoring every exchange on the inside. That costs a surprising amount of energy. Instead of grading their behaviour in silence, ask one simple question out loud. Your perception is genuinely sharp, but a clear answer from them will always beat a perfect guess from you, and it lets you put the scorecard away. One plain question, asked kindly, is more elegant than months of silent judging anyway.
text.the-talk: Your talk will be graceful. The risk is that it's so polished it doesn't sound like it matters to you. Let a little real feeling show through. I like you, and I want more than this. Is that something you want too? Don't over-rehearse it in the mirror. A slightly imperfect version, with a pause or a nervous laugh, carries far more truth than a flawless one. People trust the cracks in a voice more than the shine on a sentence. Choose a quiet place you like, somewhere beautiful helps you, and keep it short enough that the feeling stays in it.
text.your-line: Your line is carelessness. Sin Metal can't stay where it's treated as optional. Plans cancelled without care, details forgotten, effort that only ever goes one way. Decide what isn't acceptable for you, specifically. When it happens repeatedly, not once on a bad week but as a pattern, step away with grace. You don't have to fight to be valued or prove your worth in an argument. The right person notices it without being shown a list. Write down two or three things that would tell you you're being treated as optional. Then trust yourself when you see them.
text.either-way: Either way, your worth stays exactly where it was. If they want more, wonderful, let them show it with care and attention to detail. If not, it's their loss of something genuinely rare. Give yourself time and beauty, a quiet weekend, something lovely just for you, and then return to your high standards without apology. They aren't the problem here. They're a filter, and filters are supposed to keep some things out. Yours is working. Buy the flowers. Wear the good coat. Remember that your taste brought you here and it will bring you somewhere better.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You don't fall easily, Sin. They must have impressed you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And now you're pretending to be casual. Elegantly. Badly.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your standards are not too high.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You're grading every text in silence. Just ask the question.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Let a little real feeling show.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Don't rehearse it into a press release.

spring.intro: A spring jewel sits in a garden of options. Wood ruled your birth season, Sin, and Metal shapes Wood, so you have a refined eye and plenty of choice. In a situationship that can make you the hesitant one. You like them, but you're not sure they're quite right, and committing feels like closing the display case for good. Spring Sin keeps things open while quietly judging. Be honest about whose vagueness this is. If it's yours, they deserve to know. If it's theirs, your standards apply here too. You'd never accept half-effort in anything else you love.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your standards are sky high for shoes and nonexistent for texting back. Curious, Sin.

summer.intro: Summer Sin was polished in the heat. Fire ruled your season, and Fire tests Metal, so you're sensitive to criticism and very good at seeming fine. In a situationship that sensitivity turns every delayed reply into a verdict on you. You might not ask what this is because rejection would scratch too deep. So you stay perfect and agreeable and wait to be chosen. Summer Sin's lesson is that heat reveals what's real. Asking a clear question is heat. It's uncomfortable, but it shows you whether this is gold or plating. Either answer protects your shine in the long run.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A slow reply isn't a verdict on you, Sin. It's just a slow reply.

autumn.intro: Autumn Sin is the jewel at full sparkle. Metal ruled your birth month and doubled your element, which gives you strong standards, strong pride and a clear sense of what you deserve. In a situationship, pride can stop you admitting you want more. You play it cool and elegant, as if you could take or leave them. They might believe you. Strong Sin's blind spot is waiting to be chosen instead of choosing. You don't lose value by saying you'd like this to be real. You gain clarity. Say it in your own polished way, then let their answer show you their worth.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Playing it so cool they think you don't care. Great acting, Sin. Terrible strategy.

winter.intro: Winter Sin sparkles under ice. Water ruled your season and Metal generates Water, so you're perceptive, articulate and often three steps ahead in reading the situation. You've probably already worked out what this is. You just don't like the answer. In a situationship winter Sin tends to narrate rather than act: brilliant voice notes to friends, sharp analysis, no actual conversation with the person involved. Your insight is real. It's wasted if it only goes to the group chat. Take one of those perfect sentences you've said about them and say it to them instead.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your group chat already heard the speech. Maybe they should hear it too.

strength.strong: Your jewel is well set, Sin, so you know your worth and hold your standards high. In a situationship that can make you critical or distant: noticing every flaw, holding back until they're perfect. Or you never ask because asking feels beneath you. The blind spot is pride guarding your heart so well that nobody gets in. Standards are good. Let one of them be honesty, including your own. Tell them what you'd want. Being direct doesn't dull your shine. It makes it easier to see.
strength.weak: With thin support for your Day Master, Sin, your sense of worth can lean on how they treat you. In a situationship that's painful: a warm week feels like approval, a quiet week feels like rejection. You might polish yourself constantly to stay chosen. The blind spot is letting someone else's inconsistency set your value. It can't. Write down how you want to be treated, then hold this situationship up against that list. You're the measure here, not them. Their mood is just weather.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practise clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyse every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analysed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: A paragraph answered with a thumbs up
gap-wood.text: You spent ten minutes on a text to a Gap Wood and got back a thumbs up. Let's start there, because that thumbs up is the whole story of this situationship in one emoji. Gap isn't careless with you. Gap is literal. They meant yes. They didn't notice the care in your phrasing because they don't phrase things; they say them. The drift happens through hints. You signal with small precise moves: a slightly later reply, a story posted that only they would understand, a comment about how some people make plans further ahead. Gap tends to miss all of it. What Gap does notice is the critique, and that can make a tall tree go stiff. Your signal ends up reading as judgement rather than longing. For the talk, trade the hint for one clean sentence. You are good at precise; use it here: I'd like us to be exclusive and actually call it a relationship. Is that what you want? Ask in private, not over dinner with friends, because Gap's bluntness in public is one of your sore spots and you don't need that risk tonight. Clear words are not less elegant. They're just harder to misread.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, your carefully chosen words deserve better than a thumbs up.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, 'ok 👍' is not a reply to a paragraph. Try a compliment.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, hints bounce off trees. Say it plainly.

eul-wood.title: Read receipts and the pruning shears
eul-wood.text: An Eul Wood is lovely in a way you admire: easy with people, soft, a bit wild at the edges. You see potential everywhere, and you can't help mentioning how they could be even more themselves. A small note about their posture, their friend who's a bit much, their habit of being late. You mean it as care. Eul hears it as pruning. The drift happens quietly. Eul adapts to you, becomes agreeable, says yes too easily, and you can find that a little disappointing, because you wanted someone with shape. Meanwhile, you're sensitive to rejection, so if Eul pulls back even slightly, you go quietly cold, polished, perfectly polite. Nobody names the cold spell. Your texts are crafted on both sides, and both of you watch read receipts like stock prices. Your signal is critique, and to a vine it can read as not being wanted as they are. For the talk, lead with what you love, not what you'd tweak: I really like who you are. I'd like us to be together, officially. Where are you with that? Then hold back the critique for a while. Let Eul grow towards you without the scissors.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You both reread every text. Imagine just sending one.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, that 'small note' was a pruning. Put the scissors down.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, have an opinion. It's the attractive part.

byeong-fire.title: Everyone thinks you're a couple already
byeong-fire.text: 丙辛 is one of the five heavenly combinations, and with a Byeong Fire, you feel why. Byeong's warmth makes you shine. You relax around them in a way you rarely do with anyone, and they seem to genuinely enjoy your sharpness. People keep asking if you two are together. Neither of you has a clear answer. The drift tends to come from the noise. Byeong is loud, generous with everyone, and sometimes careless with the details that matter to you: the jacket you wore for them, the thing you mentioned twice, the fact that you hate surprise group dinners. When you feel overlooked, you pull back, reply later, or go quietly cutting. Byeong may not even notice the withdrawal, because the sun was busy shining elsewhere. Your signal is polish, which can read as coolness to a fire that needs response. For the talk, give Byeong something direct and quick, because quick matters to a sun: I really like you, and I want us to be exclusive and actually call it something. How about you? Don't wait for Byeong to notice your hints. Say the thing. And let Byeong see you're pleased when they get it right. It keeps the light where you want it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 丙辛, sunlight on a jewel. Everyone already thinks you're a couple.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, that joke about Sin's outfit in front of friends? Noted. Forever.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, reply a little faster. The sun notices.

jeong-fire.title: The comment at dinner with friends
jeong-fire.text: A Jeong Fire warms you without blinding you, which is rare. They're thoughtful, intense, and they look at you as if you're the only person in the room. Sometimes that's exactly what you want. Sometimes it's a lot. The drift here is two delicate people, each waiting for the other to stop being careful. Jeong's focus can feel like pressure to you, and you step back to breathe. Jeong reads the step back as coldness. Meanwhile, your sharp eye notices things, and when you mention them, especially in public, Jeong takes it as a review. Then you're both quiet, both rereading texts before sending, both wondering if the other is cooling. The 'what are we' question becomes too heavy to ask, because asking feels like exposing yourself. Your signal is poise, which can look like you're not that invested. For the talk, start with warmth, not critique: I love how you look at me. I'd like to be with you, officially. What do you say? Keep any feedback for later, for the walk home, and keep it short. And send something silly first. A ridiculous selfie can break a week of tension.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A flame near silver. Beautiful and very, very careful.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Feedback at dinner with friends? Save it for the walk home.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Send the silly selfie. Then have the talk.

mu-earth.title: Eleven hints and a mountain that missed them
mu-earth.text: A Mu Earth is a mountain guarding a gem, and you're the gem. They make you feel safe without making a fuss about it. They carry your bags, fix your bike, show up on time. It's lovely. It's also deeply unromantic in the way it's said, which is to say, it's mostly not said at all. The drift here is your hints. You've mentioned your friend's partner planning a surprise. You've posted a song. You've gone a little quieter after Mu forgot to comment on the dress. Mu has missed every single hint, not from lack of care, but because Mu takes everything at face value. You can start to feel unappreciated. Mu can start to feel like they're failing a test they were never given. And when you critique Mu's simplicity, Mu can find you hard to please. Your signal is subtext, and a mountain doesn't do subtext. For the talk, plain words save months here: I like you a lot. I want us to be exclusive and to call it a relationship. And I'd love more compliments, specific ones. Could you do that? Understand that Mu's short reply still means care.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The mountain guards the gem. Steady love, very safe.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, Mu missed all eleven hints. Use words.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, compliment the green jacket. Specifically.

gi-earth.title: Who moved the forks
gi-earth.text: A Gi Earth is the jeweller's workbench: careful hands that make you shine. Gi notices what you like, remembers your preferences, and handles you with real tenderness. You feel valued in a way that suits you. The drift here is your eye for detail. You see things that could be better, and sometimes you just fix them. You straighten the table setting Gi already did. You suggest a different restaurant than the one Gi booked. To you, it's nothing. Gi may spend the whole evening wondering what was wrong, and worry about it long after. Gi might start to feel you're cold or hard to please, and you might find Gi a bit fussy. Neither of you confronts things directly, so the tension, and the question of what you are, stays polite and unspoken. Your signal is refinement, which can read as disapproval to someone who tries this hard. For the talk, lead with appreciation, specific and warm: I love how much care you put into us. I'd like to make us official. Would you like that? And maybe leave the forks where Gi put them. It says more than you'd think.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The jeweller's workbench. Careful hands, precious result.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, leave the forks where Gi put them. Please.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, send the badly lit duck. Then say it.

gyeong-metal.title: One true sentence, one perfectly cold reply
gyeong-metal.text: A Gyeong Metal is the raw steel to your silver. You recognise something of yourself in them, the standards, the pride, the refusal to be anyone's fool, but they wear it so much more roughly. You like their strength. You hate their delivery. The drift here starts with words. Gyeong says something true in the worst possible way, and you answer with a sentence so precisely cold it could cut glass. Then neither of you speaks for a day, because neither of you apologises first. Your precision can feel like nitpicking to Gyeong, and Gyeong's bluntness can feel like being scratched. You hint, and Gyeong misses every hint, so you assume Gyeong doesn't care, when Gyeong simply didn't see it. The question of what you are gets lost between silences. Your signal is subtext, and steel doesn't read subtext. For the talk, say it plainly. It might feel unrefined. Do it anyway: I'd like us to be exclusive. I need you to tell me if you want that too. And tell Gyeong, once, kindly, how much delivery matters to you. Then let one blunt sentence slide without a cold reply.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Steel and silver. Same metal, different polish.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, true and harsh is still harsh. Sin, cold and perfect is still cold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say it plainly. Then let one blunt line slide.

sin-metal.title: The cold war nobody declared
sin-metal.text: Two Sin Metals in a situationship are the most stylish undefined thing in any room. You both have taste, both notice everything, and both are funny in that dry, precise way. Your texts are witty and full of subtext, and you both reread before sending. From the outside, you look like a couple who've been together for years. From the inside, neither of you has risked saying it. The drift for two jewels is pride. Both of you want to be appreciated, and both of you wait for the other to go first. One of you replies a little later than usual. The other notices and replies even later. Suddenly you're both performing indifference, perfectly, politely, for a week. That's your signature move: the cold war that nobody declares. Jealousy and comparison can slip in too, a story view from someone attractive, a glance at a party. For the talk, someone has to be vulnerable first, and it costs less than you think. Lower the stakes with a dumb meme the day before. Then, in person: I like you. I don't want to keep pretending I don't. Can we be together? Keep it simple. You're both too good at elaborate.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two jewels in one box. Dazzling, both of you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And both performing indifference since Tuesday. Stop.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Send a dumb meme. Then be brave first.

im-water.title: A week of planning and a hoodie
im-water.text: An Im Water washes you clean. With them, you feel freer, funnier, less polished in the best way. Im's mind is restless and brilliant, and they make you laugh at things you'd normally find irritating. You make Im feel admired by someone with standards. It's a good match. It's also one where you might plan an evening for a week and have Im turn up late, in a hoodie, with a new idea about opening a bar. That's the drift in a single scene. You care about details; Im forgets them. You plan; Im improvises. You start to feel neglected when Im drifts off into a project. Im starts to feel criticised when you comment on the hoodie. Im's bursts and silences can make you read meaning into gaps that may only be gaps. Neither of you is wrong. Both of you feel unseen. Your signal is effort, which Im may not notice unless it's named. For the talk, don't read too much into the gaps first. Then say: I love how free I feel with you. I'd also like to know we're a couple. Can we say so? And tell Im, plainly, that the details matter to you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A jewel washed in the river. Clarity and sparkle.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, the hoodie to the planned dinner? Bold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, name the details that matter. Im can't read them.

gye-water.title: Small comment, long silence
gye-water.text: A Gye Water is silver rain: delicate, intuitive and quietly beautiful. With Gye, you can be softer than usual. They notice the small things, the way you rearranged your shelf, the song you hummed once, and they reflect it back to you. It feels intimate without being loud. The drift in this situationship follows a very specific pattern. You make a small, precise comment, about a plan, a word choice, a friend. Gye goes quiet. You read the quiet as coldness and withdraw too. A week later nobody remembers the comment, only the distance. Gye's moods can confuse you, and your critiques can sting Gye more than you intended. Neither of you likes direct conflict, so the hurt sits in silence, and so does the question of what you are. You're both thoughtful texters, sometimes delayed, both overthinking. Your signal is precision, which to rain can feel like a sharp edge. For the talk, start by breaking the pattern: if you notice Gye going quiet, ask kindly instead of withdrawing. Then: I really like you. I want us to be together. What about you? And agree together that a late reply is just a late reply.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Silver in the rain. Delicate and quietly beautiful.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Small comment, long silence. You two invented this.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Name the sting out loud. Then name what you want.
